findings.claim: The last hunk inverts the duplicate-key guard: `if (stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey)) { stringMembers.Add(...) }`. Its sibling hunks use `!ContainsKey`. As written, a string-keyed member in this second member loop is never added, because a first occurrence is never in the dictionary. So the generated formatter silently omits every string-keyed member there, likely fields. Data written through those members is lost on serialization and never populated on deserialization. Base added them unconditionally, so this is a regression for code that does not use SuppressSourceGeneration at all.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.StringKeyMemberLoopReceipts.StringKeyedFieldAndPropertyAppearInGeneratedFormatter. It runs the generator on a [MessagePackObject] class with only string-keyed fields and one with only string-keyed properties, then asserts both member names appear in the generated source. On head one of them is missing.

findings.claim: The same inverted condition makes Add run only when the key is already present. If a property and a field share the same string key, the second loop calls Dictionary.Add with a duplicate key. That throws ArgumentException, so the generator fails (CS8785) and the analyzer fails (AD0001), which is the analyzer breakage the requirement is about.
